breakfast-link-pattie-or-slice-meatless.title: Breakfast link, pattie, or slice, meatless

content.title: About
content.content: Breakfast link, pattie, or slice, meatless (2233) is a vegetarian alternative to traditional breakfast meat products. Made from plant proteins, whole grains and spices, it provides a tasty and satisfying breakfast without meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Suitable for vegetarians and those reducing meat consumption.
Contains plant proteins such as soy and pea protein.
Flavor is designed to mimic classic breakfast sausage products.
Packaged in convenient single‑serve portions for quick preparation.
May be gluten‑free when formulated accordingly, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Provides a substantial amount of protein needed for muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional meat counterparts, it contains less saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and legumes contribute to digestive health and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortified with vitamin B12 and other B‑vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Completely free of cholesterol, making it a safe choice for those monitoring cholesterol intake.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Contains soy protein, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is used for flavor; people watching sodium intake should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Some versions may contain gluten; check the label if you have celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: May include preservatives and flavor enhancers; consider individual tolerances.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat quickly in a skillet, microwave, or oven. Serve with toast, vegetables, eggs, or as a sandwich filling. It can also be sliced and added to salads for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, use within 5–7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or discoloration.

chicken-or-turkey-rice-and-vegetables-in.title: Chicken or Turkey with Rice and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of chicken or turkey meat, boiled rice and vegetables (carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy vegetables) in a tomato‑based sauce. It is rich in protein, complex carbohydrates and B‑vitamins, as well as antioxidants from the vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein containing all essential amino acids.
Tomatoes in the sauce supply lycopene, an antioxidant that enhances cellular protection.
Broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables are high in vitamin K, important for blood clotting and bone health.
Rice is a staple grain worldwide and offers sustained satiety.
The combination of protein, carbs and vegetables makes the meal nutritionally balanced.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Protein from chicken or turkey aids muscle growth and repair, especially with regular physical activity.

items.title: Provides steady energy
items.content: Complex carbohydrates in rice release glucose slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables deliver vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and carotenoids from carrots help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber from vegetables and rice promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content in sauce
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Possible foodborne pathogens
items.content: Undercooked poultry can harbor Salmonella; ensure the meat is fully cooked.

items.title: Acidity of tomato sauce
items.content: People with acid reflux may find tomato‑based sauces increase heartburn.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a complete lunch or dinner. It reheats well in the microwave and can be used as a filling for wraps or tossed into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.

green-beans-canned-cooked-fat-added-ns-a.title: Green beans, canned, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans are cooked beans packed in a sealed can with added fat to enhance flavor and texture. The product is ready to eat and is commonly used in salads, side dishes, and hot meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the beans to be stored for 2–3 years without major loss of nutrients.
Added fat (usually vegetable oil) improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K present in the beans.
Green beans are high in dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.
Cans often indicate the country of origin – USA, Italy, China, etc.
Canned beans can be used in cold dishes without further cooking.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes normal digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains added plant fats
items.content: The added fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and give a richer taste.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Even with added fat, canned green beans remain relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Fat quality
items.content: If the ingredient list includes trans fats or hydrogenated oils, consumption should be limited.

items.title: Microbial safety
items.content: Bulging or damaged cans may indicate bacterial growth and should not be consumed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drain the beans and eat them straight from the can, add them to salads, soups, stews, or casseroles. They can also be quickly warmed in a pan with extra seasonings if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and use within 3–4 days.

infant-formula-enfamil-gentlease-powder-.title: Enfamil Gentlease Infant Formula, Powder, Made with Tap Water

content.title: About
content.content: Enfamil Gentlease is a powdered infant formula designed to ease colic and gas in babies. The formula contains partially hydrolyzed proteins, easily digestible carbohydrates, and prebiotics, making it gentler on a child's digestive system. It is prepared with clean tap water according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gentlease uses partially hydrolyzed proteins to reduce the risk of allergic reactions in sensitive infants.
The formula is fortified with DHA and ARA, fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
It includes prebiotic fibers (FOS) that support a healthy gut microbiome.
Enfamil Gentlease is suitable for infants from birth up to 12 months who need a milder formula.
The recommended preparation temperature is 37 °C to preserve nutritional quality.

items.title: Gentle digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed proteins are easier to break down, reducing colic and gas.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA support the growth of the central nervous system and visual function.

items.title: Healthy gut flora
items.content: Prebiotics promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, enhancing immunity.

items.title: Balanced vitamins and minerals
items.content: The formula provides iron, calcium, vitamin D, and other micronutrients essential for growth.

items.title: Support for growth and weight gain
items.content: An optimal ratio of protein, fat, and carbohydrates supplies energy and promotes healthy weight gain.

items.title: Cow‑milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite partial hydrolysis, the product contains cow’s milk; consult a pediatrician if an allergy is suspected.

items.title: Improper preparation
items.content: Water that is too hot can degrade nutrients, while water that is too cold may lead to poor dissolution.

items.title: Concentration control
items.content: An overly concentrated mixture can strain an infant’s kidneys; follow the dosing instructions precisely.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Use the opened container within 30 days and keep it sealed in a dry place.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare the formula by mixing the measured amount of powder with 37 °C clean tap water, stirring until smooth. If desired, up to 10 % of the total volume may be replaced with previously expressed breast milk, but not more.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed and use within one month. Do not refrigerate, as moisture can cause clumping.

content.title: About
content.content: Injera is a traditional Ethiopian flatbread made from a fermented batter of whole‑grain teff. The batter is left to sour for several days, giving the bread a mildly tangy flavor and a spongy, elastic texture that can be torn and used as both plate and utensil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Teff is the only grain almost exclusively cultivated in Ethiopia and Eritrea; it thrives in drought‑prone, low‑nutrient soils.
Injera is traditionally served as a large sheet on which various stews (wat) and vegetables are placed; diners tear pieces with their hands.
Fermentation lasts 2–5 days, during which beneficial bacteria develop, enhancing digestibility.
There are more than 30 regional varieties of injera, differing in thickness, color, and aroma.
Using injera as a plate reduces the amount of dishware needed for a meal.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: The natural fermentation of teff promotes growth of beneficial microbes that support gut health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Injera raises blood sugar slowly, making it suitable for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Teff provides substantial dietary fiber, aiding regular digestion.

items.title: Contains iron and calcium
items.content: Teff is a notable source of iron, calcium, and magnesium, essential for bone and blood health.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Because teff is naturally gluten‑free, injera is safe for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Teff allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to teff, ranging from skin rashes to digestive upset.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Teff contains phytates, which can inhibit mineral absorption if consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Sodium in accompaniments
items.content: Injera is often served with salty sauces; people limiting sodium should watch portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Injera is used as a base for stews (wat), vegetable and meat dishes, and as a “spoon” to scoop up sauce. It can be cut into strips, rolled with fillings, or simply eaten as bread alongside butter or honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep injera in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2–3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to a week) or freeze, reheating in the oven before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni with cheese and frankfurters (or hot dogs) is a dish made of boiled pasta tossed in melted processed cheese and mixed with sliced cooked sausages or hot dogs. It is popular as a quick lunch or snack, especially among children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as an easy, nutritious school lunch.
The combination of pasta and processed cheese provides a fast source of carbs and protein.
In Russia a similar ready‑to‑eat version is often called “macaroni for kids”.
Sausages can be plain boiled or smoked, changing the flavor profile.
Processed cheese often contains emulsifiers that keep the sauce smooth when heated.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The dish quickly replenishes glucose stores, useful for physical activity or growth periods in children.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Sausages and cheese provide animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Processed cheese contributes calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sausages and cheese supply B1, B2, B12 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible carbs
items.content: Wheat pasta is quickly digested, delivering rapid energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Both sausages and processed cheese often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Processed cheese and some sausages are rich in saturated fats, which in excess may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Ready‑made mixes may include flavor enhancers, emulsifiers, and stabilizers that are not suitable for everyone.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy should avoid processed cheese.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the macaroni until al dente, drain, add the processed cheese and stir until a smooth sauce forms. Finally, fold in sliced pre‑cooked frankfurters or hot dogs. Serve hot, optionally garnished with herbs or crunchy croutons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days in an airtight container. Keep dry pasta and cheese blocks in a cool, dry place, and opened sausage packages in the fridge.

content.title: About
content.content: The soy-based nutritional drink is a liquid shake made from soy protein, fortified with vitamins and minerals. It provides a quick source of energy and nutrients, is convenient to consume, and is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy protein contains all essential amino acids, making it a complete protein source.
The drink is often fortified with calcium and vitamin D to mimic the nutritional profile of milk.
Soy isoflavones may help support hormonal balance in women.
Because it is liquid, the shake is rapidly absorbed and ideal for post‑workout consumption.
In many countries soy drinks are a popular alternative to dairy smoothies.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: One serving provides about 20 g of protein, aiding muscle recovery and promoting satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Soy drinks contain minimal saturated fat, making them heart‑friendly.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Fortified with riboflavin (B2), cobalamin (B12) and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Added calcium and vitamin D help maintain bone health, especially for those who avoid dairy.

items.title: Gut‑health support
items.content: Some versions include probiotics that promote a healthy digestive microbiome.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy may experience severe reactions upon consumption.

items.title: Phytoestrogen content
items.content: Isoflavones can affect hormonal balance; individuals with hormone‑sensitive conditions should consult a doctor.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Certain formulations contain sugar; choose unsweetened versions if monitoring weight or diabetes.

items.title: GMO
items.content: Most commercial soy is genetically modified; look for “non‑GMO” labeling if you wish to avoid GMOs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink the shake chilled straight from the bottle. It can be blended into smoothies, used as a base for protein cocktails, or enjoyed as a quick snack between meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C. After opening, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned orange NFS (3933) consists of whole orange segments packed in their own juice with a touch of sugar and preservative for long‑term storage. The fruit retains its characteristic aroma, sweet‑tart flavor, and most of the vitamins found in fresh oranges.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned oranges are frequently used in desserts, salads, and baked goods where a stable taste and texture are required.
Unlike fresh fruit, canned segments are easier to digest and less prone to spoilage during extended storage.
The canning process preserves up to 80 % of vitamin C, which otherwise degrades quickly in fresh fruit.
NFS oranges are sourced from varieties selected for high juiciness and aroma.
Canned orange is often served as a garnish for meat dishes in Asian cuisine.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as hesperidin help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned orange contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even modest added sugar may be undesirable for individuals monitoring blood glucose levels.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some preservatives can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in persons with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned orange can be eaten straight from the jar, added to fruit salads, yogurts, desserts, baked goods, or used in sauces for meat and fish. It is advisable to drain excess juice before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if any off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato NFS is a selection of high‑quality tubers sliced and fried to a golden crisp. The product retains the natural flavor of potato, offers a crunchy texture and a light salty note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced agricultural commodity worldwide.
Roasted potatoes are a common side dish in fast‑food restaurants.
NFS (Not From Scratch) indicates a ready‑to‑eat product manufactured by standardized processes.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, but high‑starch types are preferred for frying.
Frying at 180‑190 °C creates a golden crust while keeping the interior tender.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potato provides potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Some vitamin C remains after frying, contributing to immune support.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potato contains slowly digestible carbs that give sustained satiety.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The skin of roasted potatoes retains fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Certain varieties contain beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A important for vision.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying increases the calorie density; portion control is advised for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound; avoid over‑cooking.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potato.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salt in the ready‑made product may be unsuitable for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roasted potatoes can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, used in dishes like fries, or served as a side to meat and fish. Sprinkle with fresh herbs, spices, or cheese before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent oil oxidation. Discard if the product develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese‑only taco is a classic Mexican snack consisting of a soft or crispy tortilla filled with melted cheese. The combination of a tender shell and stretchy cheese makes it a popular quick bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally Mexican tacos use queso fresco, but many regions substitute cheddar, mozzarella, or a cheese blend.
Taco shells can be made from corn or wheat flour; corn shells are considered more authentic.
Cheese tacos are often served with salsa, guacamole, or sour cream, though the basic version can be enjoyed plain.
In the United States, cheese‑only tacos gained popularity in the 1990s through fast‑food chains.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Cheese provides complete animal protein that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Many cheeses contain riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antimicrobial properties
items.content: Certain cheeses have natural antibacterial compounds from lactate and enzymes.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The creamy cheese and dense tortilla create a feeling of fullness, helping appetite control.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free options.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Most cheeses are salty, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein, the main milk protein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese tacos are relatively high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Trans fats in processed cheese
items.content: Certain commercial cheese products may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat cheese tacos in an oven, microwave, or skillet until the cheese melts. They can be enjoyed as a stand‑alone snack or served with sauces, fresh vegetables, and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared tacos in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 2‑3 days. Keep cheese fillings wrapped tightly in plastic to prevent drying.
